title: Queqiao-2 lunar relay satellite operational
summary: China launched Queqiao-2 relay to support Chang'e-6 and future south-pole/far-side missions including Chang'e-7/8 and ILRS communications.

sources.title: China launches new relay satellite for Earth-Moon communications

notes: Already flying; included as infrastructure baseline for 2025–2035 timeline.

title: Intuitive Machines IM-1 Odysseus soft-lands (tipped)
summary: First commercial soft lunar landing and first US soft landing since Apollo 17; Nova-C Odysseus tipped after touchdown near Malapert A, limiting but not eliminating science return.

title: Firefly Blue Ghost Mission 1 — first fully successful commercial landing
summary: Upright soft landing at Mons Latreille / Mare Crisium with 10 NASA payloads; ~14 days surface ops; first fully successful commercial Moon landing.

sources.title: Touchdown! Firefly's Blue Ghost Lands on Moon

title: Intuitive Machines IM-2 Athena — south pole tip-over
summary: Athena targeted Mons Mouton with PRIME-1 ISRU drill suite; landed in a crater ~250 m off target, tipped on its side; short surface life due to power/thermal limits.
notes: PRIME-1 was an early ISRU demo; limited science due to tip-over.

title: ispace Hakuto-R Mission 2 Resilience — landing failure
summary: Resilience commercial lander lost telemetry shortly before landing; laser altimeter issue implicated; hard landing/crash. Second consecutive ispace landing attempt failure after Mission 1.
notes: Exact failure date reported as early June 2025; day precision from secondary reporting.

title: Artemis II — first crewed Orion lunar flyby (completed)
summary: Crewed SLS/Orion free-return lunar flyby: Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, Jeremy Hansen (CSA). Launch Pad 39B Apr 1; Pacific splashdown Apr 10. First humans beyond LEO since Apollo 17.

sources.title: NASA Welcomes Record-Setting Artemis II Moonfarers Back to Earth
Orion splashes down to successfully end Artemis 2 mission

title: Long March 10 / Mengzhou abort & recovery flight test
summary: Low-altitude Long March 10 demonstration and Mengzhou max-Q abort test at Wenchang; sea recovery of Mengzhou return capsule. Milestone toward crewed lunar architecture before 2030.
notes: Primary Chinese state-media coverage of exact day; secondary English summaries used.

title: NASA revises Artemis architecture: LEO lander demo + 2028 landing
summary: Under Administrator Isaacman, NASA inserts Artemis III as mid-2027 LEO HLS docking demo; keeps first crewed landing on Artemis IV (early 2028) and Artemis V (late 2028); standardizes SLS; pivots from Gateway toward surface Moon Base.

sources.title: NASA Adds Mission to Artemis Lunar Program, Updates Architecture

title: Lunar Gateway paused/cancelled; HALO/PPE repurposed
summary: NASA pauses/stops Gateway as a lunar orbital station on the prior Artemis path; HALO/PPE tech eyed for Lunar Infrastructure Demo (LID) surface missions and related Moon Base work. ESA (Jun 2026): I-Hab through CDR; slow Lunar View; assess Lunar Link (Jul 2026 ITT for standalone/Moonlight-precursor studies targeting development schedules that could support Q4 2029). CSA/MDA (Aug 2026): repurpose Canadarm3 for lunar-surface ops.

sources.title: NASA, Northrop Grumman repurpose Gateway elements for Moon Base demo missions
ESA Details Next Steps for Agency's Gateway Contributions
Northrop Grumman, Canadian Space Agency repurpose their Gateway projects
MDA Space Responds to CSA Canadarm3 Announcement
ESA opens call to repurpose Gateway communications module

notes: Status remains cancelled for orbital Gateway station. International module flight assignments still unsettled; see companion events for Canadarm3 / ESA module posture.

title: NASA awards Moon Base LTV contracts (Astrolab, Lunar Outpost, Blue Origin)
summary: Astrolab CLV-1 (~$219M) and Lunar Outpost Pegasus (~$220M) selected for scaled crewed LTVs; Blue Origin MK1 delivery contract (~$188M base + options) to place rovers before Artemis IV (2028).

sources.title: NASA Provides Update on Moon Base Rovers, Landers, Missions
NASA selects four companies for initial moon base awards

title: Axiom Space / Prada unveil AxEMU LCVG inner layer
summary: Liquid Cooling and Ventilation Garment for AxEMU lunar surface suits unveiled; suits planned for Artemis IV crewed landing EVAs (xEVA).

sources.title: Axiom Space, Prada Unveil Inner Layer of Next-Gen Lunar Spacesuit
Spacesuit Development Delays Could Impact Artemis Timeline

notes: Separate from this completed unveiling: NASA OIG (Apr 2026) warns AxEMU demos slipped to late 2027 with little margin for Artemis IV 2028; Axiom (Apr 2026 Space Symposium) says NASA expects a 2027 in-space suit flight (ISS EVA or Artemis III). See axemu-oig-readiness-risk-2026 and axemu-flight-demo-2027.

title: Blue Origin Blue Moon MK1 Endurance (Moon Base I) — first cargo lander
summary: First Blue Moon Mark 1 cargo lander (Endurance / Moon Base I) to the south pole with NASA SCALPSS and LRA. Blue Origin SVP Lunar Permanence stated expectation of launch in Q1 2027 after New Glenn LC-36 static-fire anomaly (May 2026); lander held in quiescent storage pending New Glenn return-to-flight.

sources.title: Blue Origin identifies engine issue behind New Glenn explosion
NASA Provides Updates on Moon Base Cargo Landers

notes: Earlier NASA/company late-2026 NET superseded by New Glenn grounding. Year precision; Q1 2027 is company expectation cited by Spaceflight Now, not a firm countdown window.

title: Astrobotic Griffin-1 (Moon Base II) with Astrolab FLIP rover
summary: Astrobotic Griffin Mission One (NASA Moon Base II) on Falcon Heavy delivering Astrolab FLIP rover plus integrated payloads (e.g. ESA LandCam-X, Mission Control BEACON CubeRover) to the south pole region. Astrobotic (Jun 2026) says late 2026; Spaceflight Now reports Q4 2026 Falcon Heavy — no day announced. VIPER is not on this flight.

sources.title: Griffin-1 Lunar Lander Unveiled Ahead of Environmental Testing
Astrobotic showcases Griffin-1 lander ahead of environmental testing
NASA Provides Updates on Moon Base Cargo Landers

notes: Company/press: late 2026 / Q4 2026. Aggregator NET November is not used as sole source. Year precision retained.

title: Intuitive Machines IM-3 — Reiner Gamma + CADRE + Altus-1
summary: Intuitive Machines Nova-C IM-3 (NASA Moon Base designation) to Reiner Gamma with Lunar Vertex, JPL CADRE micro-rovers, ESA retroreflector, and commercial/international payloads, plus Altus-1 lunar communications relay. CEO Stephen Altemus (Q2 FY2026 earnings) stated a January–March 2027 Falcon 9 window after AIT, engine hot-fire, and an October 2026 delta FRR — slipping the earlier NASA 2026 listing.

sources.title: Intuitive Machines Q2 FY2026 earnings call transcript

notes: Company earnings call is the schedule driver (Q1 2027 Jan–Mar). NASA event page still shows year 2026 as of access — treat as outdated listing. Status slipped vs prior 2026 public target. Day not published.

title: Firefly Blue Ghost Mission 2 — far side + Elytra + Pathfinder
summary: CLPS far-side campaign ('Riders 2 the Dark'): Blue Ghost stacked on Elytra Dark; lunar-orbit deploy of ESA Lunar Pathfinder; surface delivery of NASA LuSEE-Night / JPL User Terminal plus commercial Rashid Rover 2 (UAE), Fleet SPIDER (AU), and Volta LightPort (CA). Firefly official mission page lists launch no earlier than 2027 (prior public materials said 2026 / NET Dec 2026).

sources.title: Blue Ghost + Elytra: Lunar Far Side

notes: Slipped vs earlier 2026 CLPS/ESA Pathfinder public targets. Firefly page is controlling NET year; no day published.

title: Draper APEX / CP-12 CLPS mission terminated
summary: NASA and Draper mutually ended CLPS task order CP-12 (APEX 1.0 / ispace-U.S. lander) in July 2026 after repeated lander redesigns and engine changes pushed readiness into ~2030–2031. ispace-U.S. said it expects subcontract termination and will pursue CLPS 2.0; NASA intends to fly the science payloads on later deliveries.

sources.title: ispace-U.S. Update on Contract with Draper (CP-12 termination)
NASA terminates Draper lunar lander mission

notes: Primary confirmation: ispace 15 Jul 2026 PDF; SpaceNews 17 Jul 2026. Do not keep as a 2026 flight.

title: ESA Lunar Pathfinder communications relay (Moonlight precursor)
summary: SSTL-built Lunar Pathfinder relay satellite: Moonlight precursor providing S-band lunar proximity links and X-band Earth relay. Rides Firefly Blue Ghost Mission 2 / Elytra stack into lunar orbit under NASA–ESA barter / CLPS. Multi-year commercial service life after commissioning.
notes: Tied to Blue Ghost M2; Firefly NET 2027 supersedes earlier 2026 Pathfinder materials. LunaNet interop demo remains 2029.

title: Chang'e-7 south pole survey — slipped from late 2026
summary: Multi-element south pole mission (orbiter, lander, rover, hopper) to prospect resources/ice. Rolled to pad Aug 2026 then postponed; state media: cannot launch in 2026 window. Secondary reporting points to early 2027.
notes: Official CNSA year not reconfirmed after Aug 2026 scrub; treat as 2027 planned with slip from 2026.

title: Artemis III — crewed LEO HLS rendezvous/docking demo
summary: Crewed LEO risk-reduction flight (not a lunar landing): SLS/Orion docks with Blue Origin Blue Moon MK2 and/or SpaceX Starship Version 3 HLS test articles. NASA named crew (Jun 2026): Randy Bresnik (CDR), Luca Parmitano/ESA (PLT), Andre Douglas and Frank Rubio (MS); Bob Hines backup. Up to two crew may enter the Blue Moon test article; NASA states astronauts will not enter the Starship test article. Optional AxEMU suit checkout under discussion.

sources.title: NASA Marches Toward Artemis III Mission in 2027, Names Crew Members
How NASA’s Artemis III Lander Test Will Pave Way for Moon Landings

notes: NASA architecture materials cite mid-2027; Isaacman has also said late 2027 for provider readiness. Year precision until a firm launch window. HLS provider for Artemis IV still readiness-based after this demo.

title: Uncrewed HLS lunar demonstration flights (Starship / Blue Moon)
summary: NASA expects uncrewed lunar demonstrations of commercial landers ahead of Artemis IV crewed landing; dual-launch campaign practice. Exact provider cadence depends on Starship and Blue Moon MK2 readiness.

sources.title: How Artemis III Lander Test Paves Way
Will Starship or Blue Moon be ready for 2028?

title: Intuitive Machines IM-4 — Mons Mouton CLPS delivery
summary: IM-4 delivers six NASA science/tech payloads to Mons Mouton near the lunar south pole. Intuitive Machines Q2 FY2026 earnings: still on track for late 2027 while resources shift from IM-3 completion.

sources.title: Intuitive Machines Q2 FY2026 earnings call transcript

notes: Company: late 2027 retained; year precision.

title: VIPER rover delivery option on Blue Moon MK1 (CS-7)
summary: NASA CS-7 task order to Blue Origin includes an option to deliver VIPER on a second Blue Moon MK1 by late 2027 for a ~100-day volatiles mission. Base work covers accommodations and offload demo; NASA exercises the delivery option only after reviewing that work and the first MK1 (Endurance) flight.

sources.title: NASA Selects Blue Origin to Deliver VIPER Rover to Moon’s South Pole
Blue Origin identifies engine issue behind New Glenn explosion

notes: Option still NOT exercised as of 2026-09-13 access. Endurance now expected Q1 2027 (New Glenn gate), so late-2027 VIPER science window is tighter — keep planned, not scheduled.

title: Chandrayaan-4 lunar sample return
summary: India's first lunar sample-return: five-module architecture needing two LVM-3 launches, Earth/lunar docking, south-pole soft landing (Mons Mouton candidate sites reported), ascent, and Earth return of up to ~3 kg regolith. ISRO leadership publicly targets 2028 after cabinet approval (2024).
notes: Earlier dataset used 2027–2028; 2025–2026 ISRO chair statements emphasize 2028. Keep year precision. Ignore secondary misquotes calling CH-4/5 'crewed'.

title: Northrop Grumman Lunar Infrastructure Demo (LID) missions
summary: Northrop Grumman states it will adapt HALO-derived technology into three Lunar Infrastructure Demo (LID) missions for surface power, thermal, autonomy, communications, and hosted payloads near the south pole. Aug 2026 SpaceNews coverage confirms company/CSA Gateway-repurpose messaging; NASA flight dates still unpublished.

sources.title: NASA, Northrop Grumman repurpose Gateway elements
Canceled Gateway tech for Moon Base

notes: Company concept with public LID framing; keep conceptual for dates until NASA publishes a task order/schedule.

title: Artemis IV — first Artemis crewed lunar landing (south pole)
summary: Target early 2028: 4 crew on SLS/Orion; 2 descend via Starship HLS or Blue Moon to south pole (~1 week surface, multiple EVAs). Standardized SLS config; lander provider TBD by readiness after Artemis III demos.

sources.title: NASA's Acquisition of Next-Generation Spacesuit Services (IG-26-006)
NASA Marches Toward Artemis III Mission in 2027, Names Crew Members
Axiom Space plans 2027 flight test of spacesuit

notes: NASA repeatedly says early 2028 since mid-2025; still planned not scheduled until L- date. Provider TBD by readiness after Artemis III LEO demos (Starship or Blue Moon). Suit risk: NASA OIG Apr 2026 — AxEMU demos late 2027 with little margin; Axiom still publicly targeting 2028 surface EVAs and a 2027 in-space suit demo (ISS or Artemis III).

title: Artemis V — second crewed landing / Moon Base construction start
summary: Target late 2028 second surface mission on standardized SLS; NASA says Moon Base construction effectively begins around this cadence with annual landings thereafter.

title: Crewed Lunar Terrain Vehicles delivered ahead of Artemis IV
summary: Goal to have Astrolab CLV-1 and/or Lunar Outpost Pegasus on south pole via Blue Moon MK1 before first crewed landing for scouting and crew mobility.

title: Chang'e-8 — ISRU / ILRS precursor with international rovers
summary: South-pole (Leibnitz-Beta) ISRU and construction tech demonstration forming part of ILRS basic model with Chang'e-7. Chinese rover plus international payloads including Pakistan SUPARCO ~30 kg Jinnah-1 rover; Türkiye microrover cooperation also reported. Some Chinese sources cite ~2028; April 2025 reporting ~2029.

sources.title: Pakistan rover to fly on Chang'e-8

notes: 2028 vs 2029 contradiction remains; Pakistan rover confirmed by CNSA/SUPARCO MoU reporting.

title: Firefly Blue Ghost Mission 3 — Gruithuisen Domes
summary: Six NASA payloads to Gruithuisen Domes (near side volcanic constructs) for geology/science supporting Artemis.

title: Roscosmos Luna-26 polar orbiter
summary: Polar orbiter to map resources and select landing sites for Luna-27; also intended as telecom relay. Slipped from earlier 2027 target after Luna-25 failure and program reset.

title: Chandrayaan-5 / LUPEX — ISRO lander + JAXA rover
summary: Precision landing in south-polar highlands; ISRO lander + JAXA/MHI rover on H3-24L; water/volatiles prospecting. Indian DoS reported Sep 2028 target to parliament; payloads from JAXA, ISRO, NASA, ESA.
notes: Sep 2028 from DoS parliamentary reporting — keep year precision in schema; month in notes.

title: ESA Moonlight LCNS initial operational capability
summary: Moonlight Lunar Communications and Navigation Services initial operating capability: first COM + NAV satellites targeting lunar south-pole coverage; interoperable with LunaNet. ESA: initial operations by end of 2028 after Lunar Pathfinder precursor.

title: ispace Mission 3 ULTRA lander
summary: Next-generation ULTRA lander after Hakuto-R failures; commercial lunar delivery including ispace US involvement.
notes: Schedule aggregators list 2028; confirm against ispace IR releases.

title: Firefly MoonFall lunar drone tech demo
summary: Elytra Dark spacecraft deploys lunar drones ~50 km above south pole (JPL subcontract ~$75M) as Moon Base Phase One tech demo.

title: Luna-27A south pole lander
summary: Light-class lander to lunar south pole with RTG thermal systems; site selection precursor for ILRS cooperation with China.

title: ispace Mission 4 + ESA MAGPIE rover
summary: ESA's first European lunar rover (MAGPIE — Advanced Geophysics and Polar Ice Exploration) on ispace Mission 4 ULTRA lander; south polar water/volatiles and subsurface geology. Contract signed Sep 2026.

title: Artemis VI — annual crewed landing cadence (notional)
summary: NASA states roughly one crewed lunar landing per year after Artemis V; Artemis VI+ would continue south-pole exploration and Moon Base build-out. No firm vehicle/lander assignment published.
notes: Year is inferred from 'annual thereafter' language — conceptual.

title: Luna-27B north pole lander
summary: Companion light lander to lunar north pole; informs which pole is preferred for heavier follow-on platforms and ILRS-related infrastructure.

title: China first crewed lunar landing (Mengzhou + Lanyue)
summary: Two Long March 10 launches: Mengzhou crewed spacecraft + Lanyue lander; lunar-orbit rendezvous; two astronauts on surface (~hours-scale early plan). Wangyu suits and Tansuo rover in development. Official target: before 2030.
notes: CMSA repeatedly affirms pre-2030; exact year 2029 vs 2030 not fixed.

title: ESA Moonlight LCNS full operational capability
summary: Moonlight LCNS full operating capability with remaining NAV satellites (constellation of five: 1 COM + 4 NAV) and ground segment; full commercial lunar comms/navigation services targeted ~2030.

title: ESA Argonaut-1 European lunar cargo lander (ArgoNET)
summary: First European heavy cargo lander (~1.5 t to surface) on Ariane 64 to lunar south pole; ~5-year surface life. ESA programme pages cite first mission in 2030 / by end-2030; NovaMoon materials cite Argonaut-1 in 2031. Candidate payloads include surface robotics and NovaMoon PNT station. Thales Alenia Space-led industrial consortium for Lunar Descent Element.

sources.title: ESA unveils Thales Alenia Space Argonaut consortium

notes: Independent of Artemis Gateway pause per ESA statements. Exact payload set subject to Ministerial decisions.

title: ILRS robotic station construction phase begins
summary: China–Russia-led International Lunar Research Station: multi-launch build of energy, communications, ISRU and surface infrastructure after Chang'e-7/8 and first Chinese crewed landing. Basic model targeted by ~2035; open to additional partner states (CNSA cites ~17 countries/orgs).

title: Luna-29 drilling / exploration mission
summary: Revised Russian schedule places Luna-29 around 2032 for drilling/exploration (dates have slipped repeatedly; earlier plans conflicted with Luna-28 sample return ordering).

sources.title: Russia postpones next Moon spacecraft to 2028

notes: Ordering of Luna-28/29/30 inconsistent across 2025–2026 Russian statements.

title: Luna-30 heavy platform with dual rovers
summary: Heavy landing platform with two medium rovers (~500 kg class) for 50–100 km range exploration; related nuclear power plant deployment planning for mid-2030s ILRS support.

title: Luna-28 lunar sample return
summary: Russian lunar sample-return; RAS/TASS presentations in 2026 place Luna-28 around 2036 within a 2032–2036 trio (Luna-29 ~2032, Luna-30 ~2034). Earlier statements floated 2034. Soft mid-2030s window only.
notes: Prefer 2036 when a single year is needed; keep range. Ordering vs Luna-29/30 still soft across Russian statements.

title: ILRS basic model completion target
summary: CNSA chief designer Wu Weiren: ILRS basic model by ~2035 at lunar south pole (extended model in 2040s). Chang'e-7/8 contribute to basic model. CNSA (2025–2026) cites ~17 countries/orgs plus 50+ research institutions as partners.

title: Artemis Accords — expanding international governance framework
summary: Non-binding multilateral principles for civil lunar exploration. NASA reports 60+ signatories as of 2026; continues to shape Artemis partnership roles vs ILRS bloc.

title: SLS configuration standardization (post-ICPS era)
summary: From Artemis IV, NASA standardizes SLS: replaces ICPS with new second stage options; no longer planning Exploration Upper Stage or Mobile Launcher 2 after development delays — enables higher flight rate.

title: Blue Origin Blue Moon MK2 crewed lander operational window
summary: Crewed Blue Moon MK2 (originally Artemis V+) competing with Starship HLS for early landings after architecture change; soft-capture docking tests at JSC reported Feb 2026. Readiness vs SpaceX will determine Artemis IV/V assignment.

title: SpaceX Starship HLS crewed landing readiness window
summary: Starship HLS remains primary early Artemis lander path; requires orbital refueling demos, uncrewed lunar demo, and Artemis III LEO docking test. Flight cadence of Starship v3 critical to early-2028 landing.

sources.title: GAO-26-108556: NASA Assessments of Major Projects

notes: Ship-to-ship cryogenic propellant transfer remains a hard gate before uncrewed lunar HLS demo and Artemis IV. GAO-26-108556: as of May 2026 SpaceX had not demonstrated on-orbit propellant storage/transfer; key demos already delayed >1 year when NASA re-baselined Artemis (Feb 2026), with HLS cost/schedule under review. No firm NASA-published calendar date for the first dedicated orbital transfer demo as of 2026-09-13 — see starship-orbital-refuel-demo.

title: India crewed lunar landing goal (PM guideline / ISRO roadmap)
summary: ISRO chair (2025) restated PM Modi guideline for an indigenous crewed lunar landing and safe return by ~2040, after Gaganyaan (~2027), Bharatiya Antariksha Station (~2035), Chandrayaan-4 sample return, and LUPEX. Architecture discussed as multi-module docking rather than a single mega-rocket.

sources.title: Crewed Moon mission by 2040 — ISRO chief

notes: Policy roadmap year, not a flight assignment. Distinct from robotic Chandrayaan-4/5.

title: Chang'e-6 far-side sample return
summary: First lunar far-side sample-return: lander/ascender in South Pole–Aitken basin with Queqiao-2 relay support; samples returned to Earth June 2024. Landmark CLEP success feeding ILRS science.
notes: Launch 2024-05-03; sample capsule return 2024-06-25 (widely reported). Day precision from primary/secondary consensus.

title: JAXA SLIM precision soft landing (Smart Lander for Investigating Moon)
summary: Japan's first lunar soft landing demonstrated pin-point landing technology near Shioli crater. Lander tipped after touchdown but still achieved soft-landing milestone and limited surface operations, informing later Japanese commercial/agency lander work.
notes: Completed soft landing with attitude anomaly; retain as completed demo of Japanese landing tech.

title: Korea Danuri (KPLO) lunar orbiter
summary: Korea Pathfinder Lunar Orbiter (Danuri) — first Korean lunar orbiter; ballistic lunar transfer; NASA ShadowCam among payloads. Foundation for later Korean lander roadmap (KPLL / private lander).
notes: Launch date widely published 2022-08-04 UTC; lunar orbit insertion Dec 2022.

title: UAE Rashid Rover 2 on Blue Ghost Mission 2 (far side)
summary: Second Emirates Lunar Mission rover after Rashid-1 (lost on Hakuto-R M1). Firefly will deploy Rashid 2 from Blue Ghost on the lunar far side for ~10-day surface ops: mobility, dust durability on wheels, plasma/geology/thermal measurements. MBRSC completed deployment/drive-off tests with Firefly.

sources.title: UAE Moon mission ready after Rashid 2 tests

notes: Same launch campaign as blue-ghost-m2-2026; separate event for rover science/actor visibility. Window tied to Firefly NET 2027. Aligned to Firefly BG-2 NET 2027 (accessed 2026-09-13).

title: Long March 10B first orbital flight and sea-net booster recovery
summary: Maiden Long March-10B flight from Hainan commercial launch site (2026-07-10) with successful sea-based net capture of the first stage — validating reusable propulsion shared with crew-rated CZ-10A for Mengzhou/Lanyue lunar architecture.

sources.title: China achieves first-ever controlled rocket recovery in Long March-10B maiden flight
China recovers orbital booster with Long March 10B

notes: Primary: Xinhua 2026-07-10. CASC aims to inspect/reflight booster later in 2026.

title: Mengzhou-1 uncrewed orbital debut to Tiangong
summary: First uncrewed orbital flight of Mengzhou crew spacecraft on Long March 10A from Wenchang LC-301: rendezvous/dock with Tiangong, systems validation, cargo return. CMSA targeted late 2026; secondary reporting in mid-2026 warns possible slip into early 2027 pending pad readiness.

sources.title: First Mengzhou Mission May Be Delayed to 2027

notes: LEO demo, not a lunar flight — still a critical gate for China's pre-2030 crewed landing stack.

title: LunaNet lunar navigation interoperability demonstration
summary: First lunar navigation interoperability tests among LunaNet partners (ESA Moonlight, NASA, JAXA) planned for 2029, ensuring compatible lunar PNT/comms standards ahead of Moonlight FOC and multi-provider service models.

title: NovaMoon lunar differential PNT / selenodetic station (on Argonaut-1)
summary: Proposed surface reference station for differential lunar PNT, VLBI, laser ranging and timing aboard Argonaut-1 (ArgoNET). Would broadcast Moonlight corrections for ~decimeter navigation over the south pole and help realize a lunar reference frame. Candidate payload pending Member State selection.

sources.title: NovaMoon: A New Paradigm in Lunar Exploration

notes: Tied to Argonaut-1; not yet a firm flight assignment if Ministerial payload selection changes.

title: ESA Argonaut Mission 2 cargo lander
summary: Second recurrent Argonaut heavy cargo landing (~every 2–3 years after Mission 1). SpaceNews reporting of ESA industrial briefing places Mission 2 around 2033 after Mission 1 by end-2030.
notes: Year from ESA-linked press coverage of recurrent cadence; not a firm countdown NET.

title: Korea public–private small lunar lander (~700 kg)
summary: KASA strategy accelerates a privately developed ~700 kg lander on Nuri as Korea's first soft-landing attempt around 2030, feeding technology into the larger national KPLL lander. Development schedule is aggressive (~3 years); treat as published plan with slip risk.

sources.title: S. Korea aims for lunar landings in 2030 and 2032

notes: Expert commentary questions feasibility of 2030; keep planned not scheduled.

title: Korea Pathfinder Lunar Lander (KPLL) ~1.8 t
summary: National ~1,800 kg soft lander with rover/science (~43 kg payload class) on Korea's next-generation launch vehicle (KSLV-III). Objective: autonomous pin-point soft landing and surface exploration. Documented in KASA roadmap materials shared with NASA (2026).
notes: Earlier public goal was ~2031; current roadmap materials use 2032.

title: Korea LVRAD radiation dosimeter on CLPS (Intuitive Machines)
summary: Lunar Vehicle Radiation Dosimeter developed with Korea Astronomy and Space Science Institute to fly on an Intuitive Machines CLPS lander to the south pole (~2030). Flight model targeted ~2027; supports crew-safety data for future Korean and Artemis surface ops.

sources.title: Korea, NASA partner on lunar south pole radiation

notes: Payload on US lander — listed to capture Korean contribution path.

title: Korea lunar communications orbiter demonstration
summary: KASA roadmap includes a lunar-orbit communications demonstration satellite around 2029 (Nuri-class) to mature deep-space routing ahead of Korean landers.
notes: Secondary English summaries of KASA strategy; confirm against Korean primary releases when available.

title: ILRS international partnership expansion (~17 countries/orgs)
summary: CNSA reports growing ILRS membership — on the order of 17 countries and international organizations plus 50+ research institutions — with partner payloads on Chang'e-7/8 (e.g., Pakistan Jinnah-1 rover on Chang'e-8). Parallel track to Artemis Accords geopolitics.
notes: Ongoing accession process; year marks mid-2020s partnership wave rather than a single signing day.

title: ILRS extended model target (2040s)
summary: After the ~2035 basic model, CNSA describes an extended ILRS model in the 2040s expanding south-pole station capabilities. High-level roadmap only.
notes: Decade-scale conceptual; no flight IDs.

title: Pakistan Jinnah-1 rover on Chang'e-8
summary: Indigenous ~30 kg SUPARCO rover (named Jinnah-1 via national contest) to fly on China's Chang'e-8 lander for terrain mapping, regolith analysis, radiation/plasma, and mobility tech. Pakistan controls rover after Chinese landing.
notes: Same campaign as change-8-2028; separate id for partner visibility.

title: ESA awards Moonlight LCNS industrial implementation (Telespazio consortium)
summary: At IAC Milan (Oct 2024) ESA formally launched Moonlight with Telespazio-led consortium contract for lunar communications and navigation constellation — industrial start of Pathfinder→IOC→FOC sequence.

title: ESA selects Thales Alenia Space-led Argonaut industrial consortium
summary: ESA unveiled Thales Alenia Space Italy as Lunar Descent Element prime for Argonaut, with Mission 1 proposed for end-2030 funding decisions and recurrent flights thereafter.

sources.title: ESA unveils Thales Alenia Space Argonaut consortium

title: New Glenn return-to-flight after LC-36 static-fire anomaly
summary: After a May 28, 2026 New Glenn integrated hotfire anomaly at LC-36 destroyed a vehicle and damaged pad infrastructure (BE-4 main oxygen valve cited by CEO Dave Limp), Blue Origin targets return-to-flight by end of 2026 via a horizontal/vertical hybrid CONOPS while rebuilding pad systems. Gates Blue Moon MK1 Endurance (Moon Base I).

sources.title: Blue Origin identifies engine issue behind New Glenn explosion

notes: Company end-2026 goal; not a firm countdown. Critical path for MK1 and subsequent Blue Moon cadence.

title: NASA OIG: AxEMU suit demos late 2027; margin risk for Artemis IV
summary: NASA Office of Inspector General report IG-26-006 (Apr 20, 2026) finds original 2025/2026 xEVAS demonstration schedules overly optimistic; Axiom targeting late-2027 demos for lunar and microgravity suits with little/no margin for the 2028 Artemis landing, and a historical-average delay scenario stretching to ~2031. Collins xEVAS task orders were descoped in 2024, leaving Axiom as sole provider.

sources.title: Spacesuit Development Delays Could Impact Artemis Timeline and ISS Operations
NASA's Acquisition of Next-Generation Spacesuit Services (IG-26-006)

notes: Policy/risk milestone (report issuance), not a flight. Track against Artemis IV surface EVA readiness and axemu-flight-demo-2027 (Axiom Apr 2026: in-space test on ISS or Artemis III in 2027).

title: CSA intends to repurpose Canadarm3 for lunar-surface / Moon Base ops
summary: Following NASA's Gateway pause, the Canadian Space Agency announced intent (Aug 6, 2026) to repurpose Canadarm3 investments with MDA Space toward complex lunar operations supporting Artemis/Moon Base, with possible LEO commercial-station adaptations. No new deployment date or incremental contract value published.

sources.title: MDA Space Responds to Canadian Space Agency Announcement on Canadarm3
Northrop Grumman, Canadian Space Agency repurpose their Gateway projects

title: ESA interim posture on I-Hab, Lunar View, Lunar Link after Gateway pause
summary: After the 347th ESA Council (17 Jun 2026 briefing), ESA said I-Hab continues through CDR then repurpose assessment; Lunar View slows while retaining deep-space tech; Lunar Link under assessment including possible Moonlight use. On 27 Jul 2026 ESA issued an Invitation to Tender for Lunar Link Repurposing Mission Phase 1 (up to two ~€3M Phase A/B1 studies ≤12 months); study schedules are required to support a possible Q4 2029 launch. Broader roadmap expected at Dec 2026 interim ministerial.

title: Australia Roo-ver lunar south pole delivery (CLPS / Intuitive Machines)
summary: Australian Space Agency's Roo-ver (~20 kg suitcase-class semi-autonomous rover built by ELO2 consortium) to the lunar south pole region in 2030 aboard an Intuitive Machines CLPS delivery, carrying an integrated NASA analysis instrument. Expected surface ops ~14 Earth days.
notes: ASA primary pages confirm 2030 + Intuitive Machines; year precision only.

title: AxEMU in-space flight demonstration (ISS or Artemis III)
summary: Axiom Space plans the first in-space test of the AxEMU lunar surface suit in 2027, either via an ISS demonstration (better for EVA) or as part of the revised Artemis III LEO mission with HLS providers (launch loads / pressurized cabin checkout). Venue TBD; CEO Jonathan Cirtain (Apr 2026 Space Symposium) said NASA expects to fly a suit in 2027 one way or the other. Qualification testing targeted to wrap ~mid-2027 ahead of Artemis IV surface suits.

sources.title: Axiom Space plans 2027 flight test of spacesuit
Spacesuit Development Delays Could Impact Artemis Timeline

notes: Not a firm countdown; ISS vs Artemis III path undecided. Aligns with OIG late-2027 demo risk framing.

title: ESA Lunar Link repurposing ITT (Phase A/B1 studies)
summary: Following the Jun 2026 Council posture on Gateway contributions, ESA issued a 27 Jul 2026 Invitation to Tender for Lunar Link Repurposing Mission Phase 1 studies — up to two parallel firm-fixed-price contracts (each up to ~€3M) for ≤12-month Phase A/B1 work on standalone cislunar communications / Moonlight-precursor concepts. Tender requires proposed development schedules that support a possible Q4 2029 launch.

notes: Confirmed ITT issuance; Q4 2029 is a study schedule support target, not a funded flight. Flight assignment still open pending Dec 2026 ministerial / study results.

title: Starship ship-to-ship orbital propellant transfer demo
summary: Critical HLS technology demonstration: rendezvous/docking of two Starships and cryogenic methane/oxygen propellant transfer in LEO (later campaigns need many tanker flights for a lunar-capable HLS). GAO-26-108556 reports that as of May 2026 SpaceX had not yet demonstrated on-orbit propellant storage/transfer, and that propellant-transfer and uncrewed lunar demos were already delayed more than a year when NASA re-baselined Artemis in Feb 2026. No firm public launch date.

notes: Do not treat 2026 as a countdown date — year/range reflects slipped prior targets and continuing 2026–27 planning language only. Secondary podcast/wiki NETs not used as sole sources.

title: JAXA pressurized lunar rover delivery (Artemis VII+) via Starship cargo
summary: Under the Apr 2024 NASA–Japan agreement, JAXA (with Toyota industry partnership) develops a crewed pressurized rover accommodating two astronauts for up to ~30 days near the south pole, with remote/uncrewed ops between crewed visits (~10-year life). NASA plans to use it from Artemis VII onward. NASA later assigned SpaceX’s Starship cargo lander to deliver the rover no earlier than fiscal year 2032.

title: Blue Origin large lunar surface habitat cargo delivery
summary: As part of NASA’s large cargo lander demonstration assignments to HLS providers, the agency expects Blue Origin to deliver a lunar surface habitat no earlier than fiscal year 2033, complementary to SpaceX’s pressurized-rover cargo delivery. Builds on prior NASA requests for cargo variants of crewed Blue Moon / Starship landers.

title: Intuitive Machines Altus-2–5 lunar relay constellation deployment
summary: After Altus-1 rides IM-3 in Q1 2027, Intuitive Machines stated (Q2 FY2026 earnings) it plans to deploy the remaining four Altus lunar communications relay satellites (Altus-2 through Altus-5) together in 2028 as part of its Lunar Data Network / Near Space Network services architecture supporting multi-mission cislunar connectivity.
